standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can complete a realistic task initiation task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.
scenario: The learner names one real task currently stalled because they have not started it, chooses between two starting techniques based on which fits the task better, writes down the exact tiny first action the technique calls for, and then carries out that first action for real today before recording what happened next.

simulationAlternative.description: If no real stalled task is available right now, the learner instead picks one task from their household's ongoing chore list, such as sorting a drawer or clearing off a table, applies the same starting technique to it, and records what happened using the same steps.

materials: learner-local: paper or a notes app
adult-or-local: a timer (a phone timer, kitchen timer, or clock works)

tasks.directions: Analyze the complete worked example on swk-rfl-g7-u01-l04-model-card before beginning.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Complete the fictional coached case on swk-rfl-g7-u01-l04-guided-card, use criterion-specific feedback, and finish its fresh correction turn.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Choose the permitted real-life route or complete fictional route on swk-rfl-g7-u01-l04-independent-card; follow every step and retain only the named minimal evidence.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Complete the minimal evidence record on swk-rfl-g7-u01-l04-evidence-record; omit or fictionalize private details.

prompts.text: Explain whether the technique made starting easier, about the same, or harder than usual, and say whether you would use this same technique again on a different task you have been putting off.

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g7-u01-l04-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g7-u01-l04-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g7-u01-l04-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Starting technique selection: A specific technique is chosen and justified for the task, and the first action is written as a concrete, physical, sub-minute step. | Real task initiation and follow-through: The task is actually started today using the chosen technique, and the learner reports specifically what happened once the timer or first step ended. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g7-u01-l04-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner apply the technique to a second stalled task this week and compare which of the two techniques got them started faster.

productionDepth.practicalGoal: I can complete a realistic task initiation task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.

duration.sessionPattern: 8–10 minutes model and planning, 8–10 minutes guided try, 20–30 minutes application, 7–10 minutes evidence and revision
duration.adultTime: No adult time required unless the learner chooses support

localMaterials.label: paper or a notes app
localMaterials.availabilityRule: Use only when already available, safe, permitted, and appropriate. The complete fictional route replaces unavailable real-world access.

localMaterials.label: a timer (a phone timer, kitchen timer, or clock works)
localMaterials.availabilityRule: Use only when already available, safe, permitted, and appropriate. The complete fictional route replaces unavailable real-world access.

materials.noPurchaseRule: No purchase is required. Use the complete fictional route when a local material, setting, source, or adult is unavailable.

resources.title: task initiation worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: The learner names one real task currently stalled because they have not started it, chooses between two starting techniques based on which fits the task better, writes down the exact tiny first action the technique calls for, and then carries out that first action for real today before recording what happened next.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact task initiation decision or action.
Model move 2: Name one real task you have been putting off.

Model move 3: Learn two starting techniques: the first-two-minutes rule, where you work on the task for just two minutes and then decide whether to continue, and the smallest-first-step rule, where you pick one step so small it takes under a minute, like opening a document or getting out one material.

Model check: Starting technique selection: A specific technique is chosen and justified for the task, and the first action is written as a concrete, physical, sub-minute step. | Real task initiation and follow-through: The task is actually started today using the chosen technique, and the learner reports specifically what happened once the timer or first step ended.

resources.title: task initiation action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal, constraints, and privacy boundary for task initiation.
2. Analyze the worked model and identify why its sequence meets the criteria.
3. Complete the guided case and use feedback before moving on.
4. Select the permitted real-life route or the complete fictional route.
5. Carry out the task, retaining only the minimum evidence named in the record.
6. Compare the result with the success checks and complete the correction loop when needed.

resources.title: task initiation coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: The learner names one real task currently stalled because they have not started it, chooses between two starting techniques based on which fits the task better, writes down the exact tiny first action the technique calls for, and then carries out that first action for real today before recording what happened next.
Coach direction: Name one real task you have been putting off.
Learner prompt: Name the task and estimate how many days or weeks you have been avoiding starting it.
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: task initiation complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: Learn two starting techniques: the first-two-minutes rule, where you work on the task for just two minutes and then decide whether to continue, and the smallest-first-step rule, where you pick one step so small it takes under a minute, like opening a document or getting out one material. Choose whichever technique fits your task better and write down the exact first action you will take.
Response 1 (t2-p1): I named which technique I am using and why it fits my task better than the other technique.
Response 2 (t2-p2): I wrote the exact first action in specific, physical terms, such as what I will open, touch, or set out, not a vague plan like 'start working.'

Equal-access rule: If no real stalled task is available right now, the learner instead picks one task from their household's ongoing chore list, such as sorting a drawer or clearing off a table, applies the same starting technique to it, and records what happened using the same steps.

resources.title: task initiation minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.

Reflection: Explain whether the technique made starting easier, about the same, or harder than usual, and say whether you would use this same technique again on a different task you have been putting off.

Success checks: Starting technique selection: A specific technique is chosen and justified for the task, and the first action is written as a concrete, physical, sub-minute step. | Real task initiation and follow-through: The task is actually started today using the chosen technique, and the learner reports specifically what happened once the timer or first step ended.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: task initiation supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g7-u01-l04-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g7-u01-l04-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional task initiation condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Starting technique selection: A specific technique is chosen and justified for the task, and the first action is written as a concrete, physical, sub-minute step. | Real task initiation and follow-through: The task is actually started today using the chosen technique, and the learner reports specifically what happened once the timer or first step ended..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g7-u01-l04-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

realRoute.title: task initiation — permitted real-life route
realRoute.permissionRule: Use only a safe, permitted setting and the materials already available to you.
steps: Confirm the setting, materials, and stop condition before acting.

Learn two starting techniques: the first-two-minutes rule, where you work on the task for just two minutes and then decide whether to continue, and the smallest-first-step rule, where you pick one step so small it takes under a minute, like opening a document or getting out one material. Choose whichever technique fits your task better and write down the exact first action you will take.
Complete the response prompts on the delivered independent card without recording private identifying details.
Check the result against the delivered evidence record and correct any missed step.
realRoute.completionCondition: The learner submits the minimal process record and the completed application responses.

simulationRoute.title: task initiation — complete fictional route

simulationRoute.completionCondition: Complete the same decision, procedure, evidence, and revision checks as the real-life route. No adult attests that a physical event occurred.

retry.trigger: Start the correction loop when a required step is missing, the reason does not match the condition, a safety or privacy boundary is crossed, or the evidence does not show the stated result.
retry.targetedReteach: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g7-u01-l04-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step.
retry.supportedReattempt: Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g7-u01-l04-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check.
retry.feedback: Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments.
retry.parallelReattempt: Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g7-u01-l04-retry-pair without the coach prompt.
retry.exitCriterion: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Starting technique selection: A specific technique is chosen and justified for the task, and the first action is written as a concrete, physical, sub-minute step. | Real task initiation and follow-through: The task is actually started today using the chosen technique, and the learner reports specifically what happened once the timer or first step ended.

guardianInvolvement.role: Optional coach only; no guardian attestation is required.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.
doNotCollect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations
account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

may: coach the guided and retry cards
mayNot: observe or claim a physical condition
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
